facts.raw_span: 4-week history of watery diarrhea (20 episodes per day)
vomiting
diffuse abdominal pain aggravated by spicy foods
8-kg weight loss (≈15% of body weight)
brownish macules on the hands and feet
hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk
onychodystrophy
mild hypoproteinemia and hypoalbuminemia (total protein 3.52 g/dL [normal 6.6–8.3], albumin 2.09 g/dL [3.5–5.2])
zinc deficiency (51 µg/dL [70–120])
low vitamin B12 (<150 pg/mL [300–900])
multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of brownish macules on the hands and feet, hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk, and onychodystrophy, along with the presence of multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa and numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum, is consistent with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

The patient's symptoms of watery diarrhea, vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain aggravated by spicy foods, and significant weight loss, along with laboratory findings of mild hypoproteinemia, hypoalbuminemia, zinc deficiency, and low vitamin B12, are consistent with celiac disease.

The patient's presentation of watery diarrhea, vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain, and significant weight loss, along with laboratory findings of mild hypoproteinemia, hypoalbuminemia, zinc deficiency, and low vitamin B12, and the presence of numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum, is consistent with Crohn's disease.

The patient's presentation of multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa and numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum is consistent with familial adenomatous polyposis.

The patient's presentation of multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa and numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum is consistent with juvenile polyposis syndrome.

The patient's symptoms of watery diarrhea, vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain, and significant weight loss, along with laboratory findings of mild hypoproteinemia, hypoalbuminemia, zinc deficiency, and low vitamin B12, are consistent with autoimmune enteropathy.

The patient's symptoms of watery diarrhea, vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain, and significant weight loss, along with laboratory findings of mild hypoproteinemia, hypoalbuminemia, zinc deficiency, and low vitamin B12, are consistent with an immunodeficiency-related gastrointestinal disorder.

The patient's presentation of multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa and numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum is consistent with gastrointestinal lymphoma.

The patient's symptoms of watery diarrhea, vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain, and significant weight loss, along with laboratory findings of mild hypoproteinemia, hypoalbuminemia, zinc deficiency, and low vitamin B12, are consistent with mastocytosis.
The patient's presentation of brownish macules on the hands and feet, hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk, and onychodystrophy is consistent with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

rationales.F06: Hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk are also characteristic of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
rationales.F07: Onychodystrophy can be seen in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, further supporting this diagnosis.
rationales.F11: The presence of multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa is highly suggestive of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome or familial adenomatous polyposis.
rationales.F12: Numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum are characteristic of conditions like Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, familial adenomatous polyposis, and juvenile polyposis syndrome.
